proposals.primaryEvidenceText: 1801 uttrasati 'is afraid'. 2. uttrasta- 'frightened' Hariv. [Cf. ápatrasati 'flees in terror' RV.: √tras] 1. Pa. uttasati 'is frightened', Pk. uttasaï; Sh. uc̣óĭki 'to run away'. 2. Pa. utrasta-, uttasta- 'frightened' (uttanta-, which PTSD s.v. also ascribes here, is < *uttānta-: uttāmyati 'faints'), Pk. uttattha-; Sh. uc̣utus pret. 'I ran away'. uttrasta- see uttrasati.

proposals.evidence: These survey tūse kāṭo dai/daī commands combine the pronoun, wood and the transitive burn verb. Degener independently records kāṭo wood and dai- transitive burn; CDIAL 6324 explicitly gives Shina dayoiki/dayonũ under dāhayati. Preserve the imperative spelling and long vowel, and distinguish the causative/transitive burning stem from the intransitive daj burn.

proposals.evidence: The subjectless kāṭo deī/kāṭo dāī/kāṭe dāī responses use the same wood plus transitive burn construction. Degener kāṭo and dai-, with Turner 6324 Shina dayoiki/dayonũ, support the components. Preserve eī versus āī and the wood ending -e/-o, and do not add an unspoken subject. These multi-vowel imperatives are kept separate from the ambiguous monosyllabic de give-type response.

proposals.gloss: (a girl) who was not given a dowry (dáap)
proposals.evidence: Degener explicitly defines adāpi as a girl who was not given a dāp dowry. This supports the local negative formation a-dāp-i, retaining the feminine ending and connecting it to the independently recorded marriage-payment noun; Turner 6279 corroborates Shina dāp but is not the immediate parent of this adjective.

proposals.evidence: Turner 1804.1 utthala explicitly lists Shina uthalū high/tall/loud, alongside Phalura utthālu and Sawi wuthalo. Degener and Rajapurohit uthalo high match this adjective, and the two survey ūthālo above responses use the same form spatially; preserve their long vowels. Exclude the rise/fly verbal forms and distinguish this high adjective from 1783 uttala shallow and 1899 ut-sthala shallow.

proposals.primaryEvidenceText: 1804 *utthala 'high'. 2. *utthaḍa-. 3. uttāla- 'great, strong, high, abundant' Śiś. 4. *uttāḍa-. 1. Wg. utálə 'high', Dm. uthála, Paš. uthā́l, ar. utthṓl, Shum. utthálə, Gaw. uthálå, f. uthéli, Kal. urt. uthā́la, rumb. hūtala, Bshk. úthal, ūthál, Tor. (Biddulph) ūtal, f. ūtil, Savi wuthaló, Phal. utthālu; Sh. ŭthắlū 'high, tall, loud'; K. wŏtulᵘ, kash. wathal 'high'. 2. WPah. cur. uthṛā 'high'. 3. M. utaḷṇẽ 'to be full and plump, (of fruit) to be ready to be picked'. 4. L. P. utāṛ f. 'high land, upland'.

Degener records niráno hungry and explicitly gives 2sm hano under han be; Turner 7266 lists Shina niráno and Kohistani nēruno. Preserve the survey’s vowel differences and short han ending rather than imposing the Gilgit paradigm on every dialect.

proposals.evidence: The tū oyāno hano/hino responses combine the pronoun with Degener uyáno hungry and han be, whose documented second-person masculine is hano. Turner 1929 explicitly attests Shina uyānu hungry despite the older water-seeking meaning of udanyu; retain the survey o-vowel and hino variant, without confusing this adjective with a thirst response merely from the Sanskrit gloss.
